findings.title: Conflict reconciliation overwrites newer flashcard reviews with older ones
findings.problem: reconcileProgress merges srsMap through mergeMap, which always chooses the local entry when both sides changed it from the baseline. It never compares review dates or card operations. A revision conflict therefore prevents whole-blob replacement but still allows an older grade to replace a newer schedule.
findings.failure_scenario: Two devices load a card with interval 3. The phone grades it Hard on November 23 while offline, producing interval 1 due November 24. The desktop grades it Good on November 24 and saves interval 7 due December 1. When the phone retries its save, reconciliation replaces the desktop schedule with the older Hard schedule.
findings.fix: Reconcile each card using ordered grade/undo operations or trustworthy review timestamps, rather than unconditional local precedence. Add a test where two devices grade the same card on different days and save in reverse chronological order.

findings.title: Legacy log merging discards legitimate repeated answers
findings.problem: progress_merge_log treats any stored row with the same id and correct value as the incoming occurrence when either row lacks day. Pre-change answer rows lack day and attempt identifiers. This deduplicates outcomes, not answer occurrences, and can discard the newest answer.
findings.failure_scenario: The stored history for a question is incorrect, then correct. A browser still running the pre-change app answers it incorrectly again and autosaves after the stored revision has advanced. The new incorrect occurrence matches the earlier incorrect row and is omitted. The persisted latest result remains correct, and ability is rebuilt without the latest miss.
findings.fix: Preserve repeated occurrences when merging revision-less histories. Use stable attempt identifiers where available and an occurrence-aware shared-history/prefix strategy for legacy rows; do not deduplicate by id and outcome. Add a SQL regression for incorrect → correct → incorrect with undated legacy rows.

findings.title: Legacy saves rebuild historical ability using ratings that were never used
findings.problem: progress_merge_legacy_blob replaces saved ability with progress_ability_from_log. Historical bank answers did not persist their calibrated item rating, so this function substitutes difficulty seeds. It cannot reconstruct the original ability calculation and changes readiness even when no answer was added.
findings.failure_scenario: A historical difficulty-1 bank item had calibrated rating 2000. A correct answer from theta 1200 produces approximately 1239.60, but its old log row contains no rating. Once a revision-less save takes the merge branch, SQL replays that answer at seed rating 1100 and produces approximately 1214.40 instead. An entire calibrated history is similarly rewritten.
findings.fix: Preserve historical ability as the baseline and apply only genuinely new answers using the appropriate rating information. Do not replay history whose calibration inputs are unavailable. Add a SQL test with a legitimate calibrated ability value and rating-less historical rows, asserting that an unchanged-history save preserves ability.

findings.title: Taking the greater XP total loses independently earned progress
findings.problem: The revision-less merge keeps both devices' new answer rows but computes XP with greatest(stored.xp, incoming.xp). Independent earnings share a baseline and must not be collapsed into the larger snapshot total.
findings.failure_scenario: Both devices start at 100 XP. The new app earns 10 XP on a fresh question and saves 110. An older open browser independently earns 20 XP on a different fresh question and sends 120. The trigger retains both answers but stores 120 XP instead of 130, permanently losing 10 earned XP.
findings.fix: Merge uniquely identified earning operations or baseline-relative contributions, including flashcard earnings, instead of taking the maximum total. If legacy contributions cannot be reconciled safely, require an explicit refresh/upgrade flow rather than silently accepting a lossy merge. Add a SQL test with a shared baseline and independent earnings on both sides.

assessment: Not ready to release. The new persistence paths can discard answers, overwrite newer flashcard schedules, lose earned XP, and alter historical calibrated ability. These are concrete defects not caught by the added tests. Static review only; tests were not executed.
